content.look_for: Let's look for dead wood. Dead canes are usually brown, black or shrivelled rather than green, and have no live buds.

criteria.text: Bark colour: green suggests living; brown, black or shrivelled suggests dead. One source says living wood on older canes, or on roses with bronze stems, can look brown.
Buds: plump, healthy buds suggest living wood; no live buds suggests dead.
Sunken patches or lesions on a cane may be canker, a fungal disease that kills more of the cane as it spreads, rather than ordinary dead wood.
Cut into the cane and look at the pith (the centre): white is living, brown is dead.

content.photo_limit: A photo can't show the pith inside the cane — check that on the plant.
content.confirm_question: Find that cane on your rose and look at it closely. Is it dead?
content.not_sure_guidance: Look again at the cane on the plant itself — its buds and its bark colour.
content.any_more_question: Can you see any more dead canes?
